services.name: AI & workflow automation
services.short: Turn repeated work into a connected process.
services.headline: Less handoff. More progress.
services.lead: A request should not need five people to copy it between five tools. We design workflows that move information, trigger the right action and surface the decisions that need a person.
services.focus: Start with the workflow, not the model.
services.body: We map what happens today: inputs, owners, systems, exceptions and the cost of waiting. Then we define a focused first release. Deterministic rules handle predictable steps; AI helps interpret language and unstructured content. Human approval remains where the consequences matter.
examples: Route incoming inquiries to the right team with their context attached.
Extract document fields and send uncertain results for review.
Connect requests, approvals, task creation and status updates.
deliverables: Workflow map and prioritised opportunity brief
Connected pilot with review and exception paths
Handover, operating guide and improvement backlog

services.name: AI assistants & agents
services.short: Give conversations a useful next action.
services.headline: An assistant that knows what to do next.
services.lead: Help customers and teams find answers, qualify a request or complete a task. Connect the conversation to approved knowledge and the tools that can act on it.
services.body: We define what the assistant can know, what it may do and when it must hand over. Tool access is scoped to the job. Actions that change business records or contact customers can require approval. The experience includes uncertainty and escalation, not just the happy path.
examples: A website assistant that gathers requirements before handing over to sales.
A service assistant that answers from approved material and routes exceptions.
A guided assistant inside a product or an immersive experience.
deliverables: Web or application interface and handover

services.name: Knowledge & document intelligence
services.headline: Your knowledge. Ready for the next question.
services.lead: Company knowledge lives in documents, inboxes and people’s heads. Build a way to find the right context, see its source and turn it into the next step.
services.focus: An answer should lead back to evidence.
services.body: We organise source material, design access boundaries and connect retrieval to an actual task. That might be answering an internal question, checking a document or preparing a draft. We plan for outdated files, incomplete evidence and questions the system should not answer.
examples: Search policies and working documents with source references.
Prepare a structured brief from a set of approved documents.
Extract, classify and review incoming forms or reports.
deliverables: Answer interface with references and review

services.name: Software & systems integration
services.short: Connect the tools behind the workflow.
services.headline: Make your systems work together.
services.lead: Build the interfaces and connections a workflow actually needs: internal tools, portals, APIs and shared operational views.
services.focus: A useful system is more than a dashboard.
services.body: We start with the actions people need to take. Data models, permissions, integration boundaries and error handling are designed with the interface. The result can sit alongside your current tools instead of asking the whole company to start again.
examples: Connect forms, CRM records, approvals and notifications.
Build a focused internal tool around a repeated operational task.
Give field and office teams a shared workflow with clear ownership.

services.name: AI-assisted creative pipelines
services.headline: More direction. Better creative control.
services.lead: Build a repeatable creative workflow around references, 3D guidance, generation and human review. Use AI where it supports a usable production result.
services.focus: The workflow matters as much as the output.
services.body: We combine real-time and technical-art experience with AI-assisted production techniques. Camera planning, source assets, consistent references and quality checks help connect an experiment to a practical creative process. The right workflow depends on the content and the tools you already use.
examples: Guide generative shots with a planned3D camera and scene.
Develop visual concepts with consistent references and review.
Bring generated assets into a Unity production workflow.
deliverables: A focused visual or pipeline prototype
A handover with clear quality boundaries

services.name: XR & spatial experiences
services.headline: Bring the experience into the room.
services.lead: Virtual showrooms, spatial product demonstrations and interactive training make complex ideas tangible. This is part of our engineering foundation—and a platform for future AI-enabled experiences.
services.focus: Use immersion where it earns its place.
services.body: We choose between VR, AR and mixed reality around the audience, device and environment. Interaction, 3D content, performance and deployment are considered together. AI can be added where a guide, conversational interface or connected workflow makes the experience more useful.
examples: A virtual product environment people can explore.
An augmented-reality product demonstration in a physical space.
A training simulation with guided actions and feedback.

services.name: Real-time 3D & technical art
services.short: Build the visual systems behind the experience.
services.headline: From a visual idea to a working world.
services.lead: Unity and Unreal production, shaders, tools and cinematic environments connect creative intent to interactive software.
services.focus: Craft that works in real time.
services.body: We bring environment art, technical art and application thinking into the same process. Visual direction is tested against performance and interaction needs. Selected work from Ammar’s portfolio demonstrates this depth, with authorship kept separate from company client delivery.
examples: Interactive environments and product visualisation.
Procedural materials, shaders and environment tools.
Cinematic previs and 3D-to-AI creative exploration.

articles.title: How to choose your first automation.
articles.summary: Look for a clear owner, repeatable inputs and a result you can verify.
sections: Start with a task you can describe

Choose a workflow the team already understands. Write down what starts it, what information it needs, who owns it and what a good result looks like. If the process changes with every person you ask, clarify it before automating it.
Separate interpretation from action

AI may help read a message or organise a document. Rules are often better for routing, validation and arithmetic. Combining them gives you clearer failure modes than asking one model to run the entire process.
Make the exception path visible
What happens when a document is incomplete? When confidence is low? When an API fails? A useful pilot includes review, retry and handover. These paths belong in the design, not in a future fix.
Agree on evidence before building
Decide what you will measure: rework, waiting time, handoffs or completeness. Use a real baseline. Run representative examples and compare results before expanding.
Keep the first release small
Pick one team and one bounded flow. Learn from real use, improve it, then connect the next part. A small workflow people trust is a better starting point than a broad system nobody can explain.

articles.title: An AI agent needs boundaries, not just tools.
articles.summary: Design permissions, review and escalation before adding more actions.
sections: Define the job in plain language
An agent should have a task, a scope and an accountable owner. “Help sales” is too broad. “Prepare a qualified brief from an inbound enquiry and suggest an owner” can be evaluated.
Start with the least access needed
Read access and write access are different decisions. Limit which records the assistant can see and which tools it can call. Avoid giving broad account access just because it makes a demo easier.
Put approval at the consequential step

Preparing an email is not the same as sending it. Suggesting a record update is not the same as applying it. Keep a human decision at the point where the action makes a commitment or changes something difficult to reverse.
Test refusal and uncertainty
Include questions with missing information, conflicting documents and requests outside scope. A useful assistant can say what it does not know, ask a focused question and route the task to a person.
Make the system understandable
Show the sources, proposed action and current state. Give users a way to correct information and recover from failure. Trust comes from behaviour people can inspect.

articles.title: Where AI and immersive technology can meet.
articles.summary: Use spatial experiences when location, scale or action is part of the task.
sections: Begin with the user’s environment
XR is valuable when a user needs to understand a space, inspect a product or rehearse an action. AI can add context, but it does not make an unnecessary headset necessary.
Give the guide something useful to know

An assistant in a virtual showroom could answer from approved product information. A cultural guide could connect questions to exhibit material. The experience needs a maintained knowledge source and clear boundaries.
Connect the conversation to the workflow

A question may become an enquiry, a training need or an issue to review. The interesting opportunity is connecting that context to the right team or system—not simply placing a chatbot inside a 3D scene.
Prototype before making promises

Device constraints, interaction design and content quality all affect the result. Prototype a bounded scenario, test it with its intended audience and validate domain-specific requirements before deployment.
Build on demonstrated foundations

Takhaial’s XR work provides practical experience in interactive environments. AI-enabled extensions are a direction we can explore with clients, not features we retroactively attribute to earlier projects.

solutions.name: Sales & customer operations
solutions.headline: Keep every inquiry moving.
solutions.lead: Connect the first question to a qualified brief, a responsible owner and a clear follow-up.
solutions.problem: Forms, website conversations and messages often arrive without enough context. Teams repeat questions, copy data and lose track of the next step.
solutions.guardrail: A person approves external commitments. The system should not invent prices, availability or promises.

solutions.name: Business operations
solutions.headline: Clear ownership. Fewer manual steps.
solutions.lead: Bring requests, documents, approvals and updates into a workflow people can follow.
solutions.problem: Operational work becomes fragile when its state lives in scattered chats and spreadsheets. The first opportunity is often a small, repeatable process—not a company-wide transformation.
solutions.guardrail: Missing information or an uncertain result goes to review. Irreversible actions need explicit authority.

solutions.name: Training & connected experiences
solutions.headline: When knowledge needs to become action.
solutions.lead: Explore how AI guidance, real-time software and XR can work together around training, products and complex environments.
solutions.problem: A static document is not always the best way to explain a spatial task. An immersive scene alone is not always enough either. The right combination depends on the learner, environment and risk.
solutions.guardrail: These are solution directions, not claims of certified training or validated safety outcomes. Deployment needs domain review and target-device testing.
